mainTopic: Night and מחוסר זמן for רבי יוחנן; missing the חגיגה cannot be made up; teachings on 'the crooked that cannot be made straight'.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate about two rulings of רבי יוחנן. The earlier answer only works if פסח שני is תשלומין, so רב פפא gives a new answer: for רבי יוחנן, night is not מחוסר זמן. The גמרא challenges this from רבי יוחנן's ruling about a זב who saw discharges at night and in the day. It answers that רבי יוחנן said that ruling according to another view, and that its new point follows רב יוסף. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה: someone who missed bringing his חגיגה during the רגל cannot make it up, as the פסוק says, 'What is crooked cannot be made straight.' Several אגדה teachings follow. בר הי הי and הלל discuss the meaning of 'cannot be counted', and why reviewing learning 101 times is greater than 100 times. אליהו teaches that poverty suits Israel. Finally the גמרא resolves a contradiction between the משנה and a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא about sins that cannot be fixed. A second answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier answer only works for one view of פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The previous answer works if פסח שני is תשלומין for the first פסח. But if פסח שני is its own separate רגל, that answer falls apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: [That works for the one who says] the second פסח is a make-up for the first. But according to the one who says the second פסח is a festival of its own, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא weakens the answer it gave just before. That answer only works according to one side of a known dispute about פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute about פסח שני. One view says it is just a make-up (תשלומין) for the first פסח. The other view says it is a separate רגל with its own standing. The earlier answer needed the make-up view, so under the other view the contradiction in רבי יוחנן comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'second Pesach' a month later, for those who could not bring the קרבן פסח on time
A make-up or redress for something missed
A festival in its own right, not just a make-up
What is there to say? (the problem has no answer yet)

steps.confusionAlert: The passage begins mid-sentence. The words 'this works well for...' come right before it, so the first line is the 'easy' side and the challenge is the 'אלא' that follows.

phrases.english: [that] the second is redress for the first.
phrases.notes: 'The second' means פסח שני.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
the second is a festival on its own,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֵׁנִי רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given just before this passage, which relied on פסח שני being תשלומין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier answer that settled the contradiction in רבי יוחנן by treating פסח שני as תשלומין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer depends on one side of a dispute. Under the view that פסח שני is a separate רגל, it fails and the contradiction returns.

steps.title: רב פפא: for רבי יוחנן, night is not 'time not yet arrived'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. רבי יוחנן holds that the night is not considered מחוסר זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: רבי יוחנן holds that night is not considered 'lacking time.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier answer did not hold up, רב פפא suggests a different way to explain רבי יוחנן's rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offerings cannot be brought at night. Even so, רב פפא says that for רבי יוחנן the night already counts as the day having arrived, so the person is not 'lacking time'. On this basis the two rulings of רבי יוחנן no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Lacking time': the proper time for the act has not yet come
Night, when קרבנות cannot be offered

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מחוסר זמן and whether night belongs to it becomes the center of the whole next discussion.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Rabbi Yochanan holds
night is not 'lacking time.'
phrases.notes: He means that even though you can't bring קרבנות at night, the day you were waiting for already counts as having come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was weakened in step 1 with a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New underlying principle attributed to רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the contradiction could only be solved through the view that פסח שני is תשלומין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The contradiction is solved because רבי יוחנן holds that night is not מחוסר זמן.

steps.title: A challenge from רבי יוחנן's ruling about a זב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן really holds this. It quotes his ruling about a זב: one sighting at night and two in the day means he brings offerings, but two at night and one in the day means he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said: if he saw one discharge at night and two in the day, he brings offerings. If he saw two at night and one in the day, he does not bring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב פפא's answer by bringing a different ruling of רבי יוחנן. That ruling seems to treat night differently. This step sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a זב who finished his clean days but has not yet brought his offerings. He sees new discharges. רבי יוחנן's ruling treats sightings at night differently from sightings in the day. That difference hints that the night still counts as 'before the time'.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he really say so? (opens a challenge)
But didn't he say...? (brings a source that contradicts)
A man who becomes impure through a discharge; three sightings require קרבנות

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Yochanan say so?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
If he saw one at night
phrases.notes: This is a זב who finished his clean days and then saw a new discharge before bringing his קרבנות.

phrases.english: and two in the day — he brings.
phrases.notes: He brings a new, separate set of קרבנות.

phrases.english: Two at night
and one in the day — he does not bring.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer by quoting another ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי יוחנן holds night is not מחוסר זמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's ruling about the זב treats sightings at night differently from sightings in the day, which suggests the night is still 'before the time'.

steps.title: If night were not 'lacking time', two at night should also require offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. If רבי יוחנן held that night is not מחוסר זמן, then even two sightings at night and one in the day should require new offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think רבי יוחנן holds that night is not 'lacking time,' then even with two at night and one in the day he should have to bring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge against רב פפא. It shows that his principle leads to a result that contradicts רבי יוחנן's actual ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the night already counts as the time having arrived, then the two night sightings came after his purity was complete. Together with the day sighting, they would make three new sightings, so he should bring new קרבנות. Since רבי יוחנן says he does not bring, he seems to hold that night is מחוסר זמן, which is the opposite of what רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you really think so)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא said that for רבי יוחנן night is not מחוסר זמן. But רבי יוחנן's ruling about the זב (two at night and one in the day means no new offerings) suggests he holds that night IS מחוסר זמן. The next step answers this challenge.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that Rabbi Yochanan holds
night is not 'lacking time,'
even two at night
and one in the day — he should bring!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לַיְלָה אֵינוֹ מְחוּסַּר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the זב ruling quoted in step 3 to complete the attack on step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's principle that night is not מחוסר זמן for רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב פפא's principle, the two night sightings would count as new impurity, so he should bring offerings. רבי יוחנן rules that he does not, so רבי יוחנן must hold that night is מחוסר זמן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was speaking according to another view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's ruling about the זב follows the view that night is מחוסר זמן. It is not his own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן said that ruling, he was speaking according to the one who says night is מחוסר זמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. His ruling about the זב was said according to someone else's opinion, not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 4 assumed the זב ruling shows what רבי יוחנן himself holds. The answer cuts that link: he was explaining the הלכה according to those who say night is מחוסר זמן. So his own view, that night is not מחוסר זמן, still stands, and רב פפא's answer from Step 2 survives.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it (he meant it in this context)
According to the one who says
Not yet at its proper time; the time for it has not arrived

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yoḥanan said it,
it was according to the one who says night is 'lacking time',

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 3-4 by limiting the זב ruling to another opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution: the ruling follows another view, not the speaker's own position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זב ruling shows that רבי יוחנן personally holds night is מחוסר זמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן said the ruling according to the opposing view. He himself holds night is not מחוסר זמן.

steps.title: If so, the ruling is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that according to that view the ruling is obvious, so why would רבי יוחנן need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says that, it is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 5. If רבי יוחנן was only spelling out the other opinion, the result is so obvious that it did not need to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חכם does not normally state something self-evident. If night is מחוסר זמן, it seems clear that sightings at night do not create a new obligation to bring offerings. So what is רבי יוחנן adding?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: According to the one who says that — it is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 5: it would make רבי יוחנן's statement unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי יוחנן spoke only according to the view that night is מחוסר זמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to that view the ruling is self-evident, so there would be no reason to state it.

steps.title: He needed to teach the case of one at night and two in the day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן needed to state the case that mixes day and night sightings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of two in the day and one at night was necessary for him to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 6. One part of רבי יוחנן's ruling was not obvious, and he needed to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even according to the view that night is מחוסר זמן, the mixed case, with one sighting at night and two in the day, could have gone either way. That is the new point רבי יוחנן was teaching. The next step explains why someone might have gotten it wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to teach this)
A sighting; an emission of a זב

phrases.english: Two in the day and one at night
phrases.notes: This seems to point back to the case in Step 3 where one sighting was at night and two were in the day.

phrases.english: was necessary for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by identifying the case that needed teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the non-obvious part of the statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ruling is obvious according to that view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mixed day and night case was not obvious and needed to be taught.

steps.title: Why the mixed case was needed: רב יוסף, not רב שישא
steps.stepSummary: Without רבי יוחנן's ruling we might have followed רב שישא בריה דרב אידי, who sees no difference between one or two sightings at night. רבי יוחנן teaches that the הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought to follow the strong objection of רב שישא בריה דרב אידי. So he teaches us that the הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what mistake רבי יוחנן was preventing. It shows which earlier opinion he is siding with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי objected that one sighting at night and two sightings at night should be treated the same. רב יוסף holds that the first sighting only gives the status of a בעל קרי, so there is a real difference between one sighting at night and two. רבי יוחנן's ruling teaches that we follow רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's זב ruling follows the view that night is מחוסר זמן. Its new point is that one sighting at night differs from two, as רב יוסף holds. His own view, that night is not מחוסר זמן, stays in place.

phrases.english: It might have entered your mind to say

phrases.aramaic: כְּאַתְקַפְתָּא דְּרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי,
phrases.english: like the strong objection of Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi,
so he teaches us that it follows Rav Yosef.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason the case in Step 7 needed to be taught.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the statement rules between two earlier opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Follow רב שישא בריה דרב אידי: one or two sightings at night are the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה follows רב יוסף, so one sighting at night differs from two.

steps.title: Missing the רגל cannot be made up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. Someone who let the רגל pass without bringing his חגיגה does not have to make it up, and the פסוק of מְעֻוָּת is said about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the רגל passed and he did not bring his חגיגה, he is not responsible to make it up. About this it says: 'What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's line about a person who missed bringing his חגיגה during the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the רגל, including its days of תשלומין, is over, the chance to bring the חגיגה is gone. He does not owe it afterward. The משנה ties this to the פסוק in קהלת: a lost chance cannot be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought the חגיגה offering for the festival
Responsibility to make good or replace

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that some מצוות are tied to a fixed time. Once that time passes, there is no debt left, only a lost chance.

phrases.english: If the festival passed and he did not celebrate it,
phrases.notes: Here 'celebrate' means bringing the חגיגה offering.

phrases.english: he is not responsible to make it up,
and about this it is said:
'What is crooked cannot be made straight,
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:15

phrases.english: and what is lacking cannot be counted.'

steps.triggerLanguage: עָבַר הָרֶגֶל וְלֹא חָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the זב discussion and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the רגל has passed, someone who did not bring his חגיגה does not have to make it up.

steps.title: בר הי הי: the word should have been 'filled'
steps.stepSummary: בר הי הי tells הלל that if the פסוק is about a missing offering, it should have said 'be filled,' not 'be counted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הי הי said to הלל: This word 'be counted' should have been 'be filled.'
steps.whatsHappening: בר הי הי challenges how the משנה reads the פסוק. The word does not seem to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A missing offering is something you would want to 'fill in.' It is not something you 'count.' So the word לְהִמָּנוֹת suggests the פסוק is talking about something else.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר הֵי הֵי לְהִלֵּל:
phrases.english: Bar Hei Hei said to Hillel:
This word 'be counted',
it should have said 'be filled'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר הֵי הֵי לְהִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's use of the פסוק from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'what is lacking cannot be counted' as being about a missed חגיגה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A missing offering would be described as something that cannot be 'filled,' not 'counted.'

steps.title: The פסוק is about someone left out of his friends' group for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: בר הי הי explains that the פסוק talks about someone whose friends were counted together for a מצוה while he was not counted with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is about someone whose friends were counted together for a מצוה, and he was not counted with them.
steps.whatsHappening: בר הי הי offers a new reading of the פסוק that fits the word 'counted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Counted' fits a person who missed joining a group being counted together for a מצוה. His friends did the מצוה as a group. He was not counted with them, and that lost chance cannot be made up.

keyTerms.meaning: For a matter of a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק of מְעֻוָּת applies to a lost chance to do a מצוה. בר הי הי reads 'counted' as being left out of the group that was counted for the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rather, this is one whose friends were counted together
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא has the word in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, reads 'his friends were counted.'

phrases.english: for a matter of a מצוה,
and he was not counted with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא זֶה שֶׁנִּמְנוּ חֲבֵירָיו לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reading of the פסוק that answers the word problem raised in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the פסוק that fits its exact word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is about a missing offering that cannot be made up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is about someone not counted with his friends for a מצוה, a chance that is lost for good.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the reading of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains 'crooked' as missing קריאת שמע or תפלה, and 'missing' as not being counted with friends for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: 'What is crooked cannot be fixed' means someone who missed the morning or evening קריאת שמע, or the morning or evening תפלה. 'What is missing cannot be counted' means someone whose friends were counted together for a מצוה, but he was not counted with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing בר הי הי just said, which backs up his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, בר הי הי read 'cannot be counted' as being left out when friends are counted for a מצוה. The ברייתא says the exact same thing, so his reading is supported. It also gives new examples for the first half of the פסוק: missing קריאת שמע or תפלה at its set time.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this way (a support)
Something crooked, bent out of shape

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא confirms בר הי הי: 'cannot be counted' means being left out when your friends join together for a מצוה.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
"What is crooked cannot be fixed"
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:15

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁבִּיטֵּל קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁל שַׁחֲרִית,
phrases.english: this is one who missed the morning קריאת שמע,
or the evening קריאת שמע,
or who missed the morning prayer
or the evening prayer.
"And what is missing cannot be counted"
this is one whose friends were counted together for a מצוה
and he was not counted with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation בר הי הי gave in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: בר הי הי's reading of 'cannot be counted' as being left out of a group counted for a מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explains both halves of the פסוק in קהלת.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק in מלאכי seem to repeat itself?
steps.stepSummary: בר הי הי asks הלל why the פסוק says 'righteous and wicked' and also 'serves God and does not serve Him', since these seem the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הי הי said to הלל: What does the פסוק mean, 'Then you will again see the difference between a righteous person and a wicked one, between one who serves God and one who did not serve Him'? 'Righteous' is the same as 'one who serves God', and 'wicked' is the same as 'one who did not serve Him'!
steps.whatsHappening: A new conversation starts. בר הי הי points out that a פסוק in מלאכי seems to say the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists two pairs. If 'righteous' just means 'serves God' and 'wicked' just means 'does not serve Him', the second pair adds nothing. בר הי הי wants to know what new idea the second pair is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק mean? (asking about a פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר הֵי הֵי לְהִלֵּל,
phrases.english: Bar Hei Hei said to Hillel,
what is the meaning of what is written:
"Then you will again see the difference between a righteous person and a wicked one,
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:18

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עוֹבֵד אֱלֹהִים לַאֲשֶׁר לֹא עֲבָדוֹ״,
phrases.english: between one who serves God and one who did not serve Him"
"righteous" is the same as "one who serves God",
"wicked" is the same as "one who did not serve Him"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר הֵי הֵי לְהִלֵּל, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new exchange between בר הי הי and הלל, about a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the פסוק in מלאכי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second pair of words seems to repeat the first pair, so it looks like extra wording.

steps.title: Both are צדיקים, but one reviewed one more time
steps.stepSummary: הלל answers that 'served Him' and 'did not serve Him' are both complete צדיקים; the difference is reviewing learning 100 times versus 101 times.
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל said to him: 'Served Him' and 'did not serve Him' are both completely righteous people. But someone who reviews his learning a hundred times cannot be compared to someone who reviews it a hundred and one times.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל answers that the second pair is not about wicked people at all. It compares two complete צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first pair, righteous and wicked, is a big difference. The second pair is a small one: both are fully righteous, but one reviewed one extra time. So the פסוק is not repeating itself; it teaches that even this small extra effort counts.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Did not serve Him' here does NOT mean a wicked person. According to הלל, he is a complete צדיק who reviewed his learning 100 times instead of 101.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is הלל answering.

phrases.english: "served Him" and "did not serve Him"
both of them are completely righteous people,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה שׁוֹנֶה פִּרְקוֹ מֵאָה פְּעָמִים,
phrases.english: and one who reviews his learning a hundred times cannot be compared
to one who reviews his learning a hundred and one times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״עֲבָדוֹ״ וְ״לֹא עֲבָדוֹ״ — תַּרְוַיְיהוּ צַדִּיקֵי גְּמוּרֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra wording in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the second pair of words a different meaning, so nothing is repeated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both pairs talk about righteous versus wicked, so the second pair is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second pair compares two complete צדיקים: one who reviewed 101 times and one who reviewed 100 times.

steps.title: Just for one time, he is called 'did not serve Him'?
steps.stepSummary: בר הי הי is surprised that missing a single extra review would earn the label 'did not serve Him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הי הי said to him: Because of just one time, the פסוק calls him 'one who did not serve Him'?
steps.whatsHappening: בר הי הי pushes back on הלל's answer. Calling someone 'did not serve Him' over one review seems far too harsh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל's answer means a difference of only one review out of a hundred gets a very strong label. בר הי הי asks whether such a tiny difference can really be that important.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now it is בר הי הי speaking again.

phrases.english: And because of one time
it calls him "did not serve Him"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמִשּׁוּם חַד זִימְנָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״לֹא עֲבָדוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges הלל's answer from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: הלל's claim that one extra review is the difference between 'served' and 'did not serve'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One missing review seems too small to deserve such a strong label.

steps.title: Proof from the donkey drivers' prices
steps.stepSummary: הלל says yes, and proves it from donkey drivers: ten parsahs cost one זוז, but eleven parsahs cost two.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. Go and learn from the donkey drivers' market: ten parsahs cost one זוז, eleven parsahs cost two זוזים.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל holds his ground and brings an example from everyday life to show that one 'extra' can make a big difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going just one parsah past the usual ten doubles the price. So going one step beyond the normal amount is worth much more than its size suggests. In the same way, the 101st review stands out and earns the title 'served Him'.
steps.whatToRemember: Going even one step beyond the normal amount in learning counts as a whole different level of serving הקב"ה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
go and learn from the market of donkey drivers:
ten parsahs for one זוז,
eleven parsahs for two זוזים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, צֵא וּלְמַד מִשּׁוּק שֶׁל חֲמָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stands by his claim ('אִין') and proves it with a real-life comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One extra review is too small to matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Going beyond the normal amount, even by one, is a major difference, like the doubled price for an eleventh parsah.

steps.title: אליהו: הקב"ה found only poverty to give Israel
steps.stepSummary: אליהו explains the פסוק 'I tested you in the furnace of poverty' to mean that out of all good qualities, הקב"ה found only poverty to give Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said to בר הי הי (and some say, to רבי אלעזר): What does the פסוק mean, 'Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of poverty'? It teaches that הקב"ה went through all the good qualities to give to Israel, and found only poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from אליהו about a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says Israel was 'chosen' or 'tested' in the furnace of עוני, poverty. אליהו reads this as saying that poverty was the one good quality הקב"ה chose for Israel out of all the options. The surprise is that poverty is counted as something good.

keyTerms.meaning: I have refined you (like metal in fire)

steps.confusionAlert: Poverty here is treated as a good quality given to Israel, not as a punishment.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵלִיָּהוּ לְבַר הֵי הֵי,
phrases.english: Eliyahu said to Bar Hei Hei,
and some say, to Rabbi Elazar:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:10

phrases.english: I have tested you in the furnace of poverty"
This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, searched

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל מִדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת לִיתֵּן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: through all the good qualities to give to Israel,
and found only poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵלִיָּהוּ לְבַר הֵי הֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, linked to the previous one through the name בר הי הי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Out of all good qualities, הקב"ה found poverty to be the one to give Israel.

steps.title: A popular saying: poverty suits the Jews
steps.stepSummary: שמואל (or רב יוסף) says this is what people mean when they say poverty suits the Jews like a red bridle on a white horse.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said, and some say רב יוסף: This is what people say: Poverty suits the Jews like a red bridle on a white horse.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל, or רב יוסף, connects אליהו's teaching to a well-known saying, which backs it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו said poverty is a good quality for Israel. The popular saying says the same: poverty looks good on the Jews, the way a red bridle looks good on a white horse. So everyday wisdom agrees with the teaching.
steps.whatToRemember: Poverty is described as fitting and good for the Jewish people, both by אליהו and by a popular saying.

phrases.english: Shmuel said, and some say Rav Yosef,
this is what people say:
Poverty suits the Jews
like a red bridle on a white horse.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up אליהו's teaching from Step 17 with a popular saying.
steps.raayaObject: אליהו's teaching that poverty is the good quality given to Israel.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A well-known saying quoted by שמואל or רב יוסף.

steps.title: The משנה: the crooked one is a man who fathers a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says the 'crooked that cannot be made straight' is someone who had forbidden relations and fathered a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: Who is 'the crooked that cannot be made straight'? It is a man who has relations with a forbidden woman and has a ממזר child from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line from the משנה so it can study it closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says some damage cannot be fixed. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא applies it to a sin that leaves a permanent result: a ממזר child, who stays a ממזר forever.

keyTerms.meaning: The crooked that cannot be made straight (קהלת 1:15)
A woman forbidden to a man by the Torah's laws of forbidden relations
A child born from certain forbidden relations; this status is permanent

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵי זֶה הוּא ״מְעֻוָּת לֹא יוּכַל לִתְקוֹן״
phrases.english: Who is "the crooked that cannot be made straight"?
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:15

phrases.english: This is one who has relations with a forbidden woman
and fathered a mamzer from her, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר: אֵי זֶה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about poverty and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'crooked that cannot be made straight' is someone whose forbidden relations produced a ממזר.

steps.title: Inference: only if a child was born
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely: if a child was born it cannot be fixed, which implies that if no child was born it can be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he fathered a child, yes, it cannot be fixed. If he did not father a child, no, it can be fixed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the exact wording of the משנה. This is setting up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions fathering a ממזר, so the גמרא infers that the child is what makes it unfixable. Without a child, the sin should be fixable through תשובה.

phrases.english: If he fathered a child, yes, it cannot be fixed;
if he did not father one, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹלִיד — אִין, לֹא הוֹלִיד — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the משנה quoted in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the 'unfixable' status depend on a child being born?

steps.title: Contradiction: sinning with a married woman can never be fixed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן מנסיא saying that a thief or robber can return what he took, but a man who sins with an אשת איש can never fix it, even with no child.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: A man who steals can give back what he stole and make it right. A man who robs can give back what he robbed and make it right. But a man who has relations with a married woman and makes her forbidden to her husband is driven out of the world and is gone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 20 with another teaching from the same תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says the sin itself is unfixable, because the woman is now forbidden to her husband forever. That is true even when no child is born, which contradicts what we inferred from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
One who robs openly, by force
Driven out of the world; he has no way to repair it

steps.confusionAlert: Both statements belong to the same רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. The problem is that he seems to contradict himself, not that two תנאים disagree.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
If a person steals,
it is possible for him to return what he stole and make it right;
if a person robs,
it is possible for him to return what he robbed and make it right;
but one who has relations with a married woman
and makes her forbidden to her husband
is driven out of the world and is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference of step 20 using another statement of the same תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that without a child, the sin can be fixed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן מנסיא calls sinning with an אשת איש unfixable even with no child, because she is permanently forbidden to her husband.

steps.title: Only someone once straight can be called crooked
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן יוחי says that 'crooked' only fits someone who was once straight: a תלמיד חכם who left Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: Nobody says 'inspect the camel' or 'inspect the pig.' They say 'inspect the lamb.' And who is the crooked one? A תלמיד חכם who left the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a different תנא, who explains the פסוק in a completely different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only check a lamb for blemishes, because a camel or pig could never be a קרבן anyway. In the same way, you only call someone 'crooked' if he was once straight. So the פסוק is about a תלמיד חכם who abandoned his learning.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb, an animal fit to be a קרבן

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
One does not say, "Inspect the camel," "Inspect the pig,"
rather, "Inspect the lamb."
And who is this?
phrases.notes: He means: who is the 'crooked' one in the פסוק?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: This is a Torah scholar who left the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: אֵין אוֹמֵר בַּקְּרוּ גָּמָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second תנא who reads the פסוק differently from רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Crooked' fits only someone who was once straight, meaning a תלמיד חכם who left Torah.

steps.title: Two verses about the scholar who wanders away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן לקיש brings two פסוקים about a תלמיד חכם who leaves Torah: a bird wandering from its nest, and ה׳ asking why the fathers went far from Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן לקיש said: About every תלמיד חכם who leaves the Torah, the פסוק says: 'Like a bird wandering from its nest, so is a man who wanders from his place.' And it also says: 'What wrong did your fathers find in Me, that they went far from Me?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן לקיש supports רבי שמעון בן יוחי's idea with two פסוקים. After this, the גמרא will answer the contradiction from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים describe someone who left a place he belonged to. That fits a scholar who was close to Torah and then walked away, so his loss is greater.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of 'the crooked that cannot be fixed': רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says it is a sin that leaves permanent damage, and רבי שמעון בן יוחי says it is a תלמיד חכם who left Torah. The contradiction inside רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's words (step 21) is answered in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Any Torah scholar who leaves the Torah,
about him the verse says:
"Like a bird wandering from her nest,
phrases.notes: משלי 27:8

phrases.english: so is a man who wanders from his place,"
and it also says:
"What wrong did your fathers find in Me,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:5

phrases.english: that they went far from Me?"

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reading in step 22 with פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That a תלמיד חכם who leaves Torah is especially faulted.

steps.title: Two different cases: his unmarried sister versus a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction. The משנה is about relations with his unmarried sister, which can be fixed if no child is born. The ברייתא is about an אשת איש, which can never be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. Here (the משנה) is about his unmarried sister. There (the ברייתא) is about a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא. It says they are talking about two different kinds of forbidden relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה hinted that with no child, the sin can be fixed. That fits his unmarried sister, since no husband was harmed. The ברייתא said 'never fixable,' and that fits an אשת איש. So both statements of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the standard opening of an answer
Here... there: splitting two sources into two different cases

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say that relations with one's sister are a light sin. Both cases are severe forbidden relations. The only difference is whether the sin can be fixed when no child was born.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is about his unmarried sister;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה, which hinted that with no child the sin can be fixed.

phrases.english: there, it is about a married woman.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא, which said it can never be fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בַּאֲחוֹתוֹ פְּנוּיָה, כָּאן בְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 21 between the ברייתא and the inference from the משנה in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different kind of forbidden woman.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה and the ברייתא were talking about the same kind of sin, so they seemed to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about an unmarried sister, which can be fixed if no child is born. The ברייתא is about an אשת איש, which can never be fixed.

steps.title: A second answer: both sources are about a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another answer. Both the משנה and the ברייתא are about an אשת איש, and the difference between them will be explained in a different way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: both this and that are about a married woman, and it is still not a contradiction. Here...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second, different answer to the same contradiction. It is setting up the next move: the actual split between the two sources comes right after this section ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer split the sources by the kind of woman. This new answer keeps the same woman in both, an אשת איש. So it must find a different difference between the משנה and the ברייתא. That difference is given in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second, alternate answer
This and that: both sources together

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
this and that are both about a married woman,
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means both the משנה and the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult: here...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא בְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer in place of step 24. Both sources are kept as talking about an אשת איש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate split: the same kind of woman in both sources, with a different distinguishing factor that comes in the continuation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After step 24, one might think the only way to settle the contradiction is to say the sources are about different women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if both sources are about an אשת איש, there is still no contradiction. The distinguishing detail follows in the continuation.
